# ECN-2026-048 - Change notice - Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-IH01

Reason for change
This engineering change notice documents a required safety and reliability correction to the cooling system of the Ring Rolling induction billet heater identified as EQ-P2-L2-IH01. Field inspection and operational trend review identified that coil cooling water flow had been marginal during several production shifts, creating risk of coil overheating and premature insulation degradation. The change clarifies the minimum allowable coil cooling water flow for EQ-P2-L2-IH01, updates machine-level controls and alarms, and amends maintenance and operator procedures to enforce the minimum flow requirement identified below.

The immediate goal is to eliminate ambiguity in operational limits, reduce forced outages attributable to coil damage, and ensure consistent implementation of protective interlocks and maintenance verification steps. This change is based on the technical assessment recorded in ECN-2026-012 and aligns required maintenance actions with documented procedures MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1 and operational steps in SOP-P2-L2-04.

Affected items
- Induction heater EQ-P2-L2-IH01: coil cooling system operational parameters, PLC alarm settings, and HMI display labels.
- Operator procedure SOP-P2-L2-04: operator checks and start-up checklist entries that reference cooling system acceptance criteria.
- Maintenance instruction MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1: preventive checks and acceptance criteria for returned-to-service verification after any cooling system work.
- Machine documentation set and visible nameplate/labeling on EQ-P2-L2-IH01 where cooling flow minimum is displayed.

Mandatory requirement
- The coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 81 L/min.

Implementation
Scope
The implementation applies to EQ-P2-L2-IH01 and associated PLC/HMI, the operator start-up and monitoring workflow, and the preventive maintenance checklist for the heater coil cooling system. Implementation steps are staged to ensure safety interlocks remain active during work and to provide clear traceable records of modifications.

Control changes
- PLC configuration will be updated to enforce the coil cooling water flow minimum. The PLC logic will inhibit heater enable if measured flow is below the mandatory value and will log the inhibit condition to the historian and maintenance log.
- HMI screens and local nameplate labels at EQ-P2-L2-IH01 will be updated to display the mandatory coil cooling water flow minimum value and the failure action that will occur if the flow is not met.
- Alarm thresholds and alarm text will reference the mandatory value and direct operators to SOP-P2-L2-04 for corrective action.

Procedure updates
- SOP-P2-L2-04 will be revised to include the mandatory cooling water flow minimum in the pre-start checklist and in the corrective actions section when low flow is detected. The procedure will direct operators to note the flow reading and to notify maintenance per the existing escalation path documented in MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1.
- MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1 will be revised to include acceptance verification steps after corrective work on the cooling circuit, requiring confirmation that flow meets the mandatory value prior to returning EQ-P2-L2-IH01 to service. Records of flow verification must be entered into the equipment maintenance record.

Physical modifications
- Where necessary, the existing flow transmitter and its calibration will be verified against one of the calibrated test units kept by maintenance. Any adjustments shall be performed according to calibration best practices and be recorded in the equipment calibration log referenced in MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1.
- A durable label stating the mandatory cooling flow value will be affixed adjacent to the local flow display on EQ-P2-L2-IH01.

Examples of operator actions
- During start-up, the operator verifies flow reading on the HMI. If the reading is at or above the mandatory value, proceed as per SOP-P2-L2-04.
- If the reading is below the mandatory value, the heater will remain inhibited. The operator follows the corrective action steps in SOP-P2-L2-04 and notifies maintenance. Maintenance will inspect cooling circuit, verify transmitter operation, and perform corrective repairs in accordance with MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1 prior to re-enabling the heater.

Records to keep
- PLC change request and configuration export for the PLC update, archived in the control systems change folder and referenced to this ECN.
- HMI screen revision package and digital photo of updated local nameplate for EQ-P2-L2-IH01.
- SOP-P2-L2-04 revision with change log entry that references this ECN.
- MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1 revision with change log entry that references this ECN.
- Maintenance verification records showing flow measurements taken after any corrective action, filed in the equipment maintenance record for EQ-P2-L2-IH01.
- Calibration certificate and verification record for the flow transmitter used for acceptance checks, filed per MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1.
- Incident reports and historian logs of any PLC inhibits or alarms that reference the low coil cooling flow condition.

Timing and coordination
Implementation will be coordinated with production planning and the control systems group to minimize impact on plant operations. All PLC and HMI changes shall be tested in the control systems lab or test environment prior to deployment on EQ-P2-L2-IH01. Procedure and maintenance document updates shall be published through the document control system and operators and maintenance personnel shall receive sign-off training on the revisions before enforced use.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-012
- MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1
- SOP-P2-L2-04

Approvals
This ECN requires signatures from the equipment owner, plant operations manager, maintenance lead, and control systems engineer before implementation. Approved revisions to SOP-P2-L2-04 and MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1 must be attached to the ECN package in the document control system prior to field changes.
